scope: Review evidence for next original-client 2FA slice; no 2FA parity claim

findings.finding: CODE_CORRECT closes the security dialog and sends CS_LOGIN_REQ again using the login form credentials. The client drives the second login.
Original security confirmation adds a MAC-address trust record and sends only CS_SECURITYRESULT_ACK; it does not allocate a session or send a deferred CS_LOGIN_ACK.
LR_SECURITY challenge issuance branch is inside a block comment in this source snapshot. Presence of the handler/client reader is not proof this deployment enabled the branch.

Current modern confirmation sends SECURITYRESULT then completes a session and sends LOGIN_ACK. That conflicts with the source client retry and can cause a duplicate login. It trusts IP before session completion in separate transactions and does not require awaiting_security before VerifySecurityCode.
Current one-use row lock works, but bTries is only incremented; no bound/expiry. CompleteSecurityLogin lacks fresh ban/agreement/site-code checks and produces incomplete ACK state.

TSECURECODE has five nullable source columns, but no matching MAC-address/security-code helper module was found by name/definition scan. TUSEREMAIL/TUSERTRUSTEDIP are explicit modern extensions. Do not assign invented historical expiry or hardware-trust semantics.

Current login sender includes three empty Zombie strings; server MAC parse is commented out. A persisted hardware trust identity cannot be inferred from these packets. A connection-bound retry grant is an explicit modern policy; do not pretend IP trust is historical MAC trust.

Normal initial login applies GetSHA1String(form password), but CODE_CORRECT retries SendCS_LOGIN_REQ with the form password directly; the sender does no hashing. Retry also omits explicit site-code argument. A byte-identical credential/site-code retry cannot be assumed. The disabled source challenge branch and unknown executable mean this path needs an explicit source-client adapter/fixture, not a general plaintext fallback.

next_acceptance: Original source client sequence: LOGIN -> SECURITYCONFIRM_REQ -> SECURITYCONFIRM_ACK -> SECURITYRESULT_ACK -> client LOGIN retry -> LOGIN_ACK; no unsolicited deferred login acknowledgement.

Bind the verification challenge to the pending connection and account; consume verification and narrowly scoped retry permission atomically. Do not grant broad IP/device trust merely because a code matched.
Retry must revalidate current credentials, bans, agreement, site code, slots/premium and duplicate rules in the existing auth transaction.
Introduce expiry/attempt policy in new numbered migration 010+, explicitly as a modern application policy rather than guessed historical data.
Use a local fake mail sink and real encrypted TCP peer; test two pending connections, wrong/expired/replayed code, interleaved ban/agreement changes, disconnect and failover. No external email.

Model the source client raw-form-password retry separately from normal SHA1 wire credentials; any normalization must be restricted to the verified pending challenge/connection and supported profile, while preserving stored bcrypt policy. Test account switching and wrong credential after confirmation; direct-login/site-code profile needs independent evidence.
